chunks: As for what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Abī al-ʿAlāʾ, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who does not know whether he has prayed two rakʿahs or one. He said: He completes it.

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abā ʿAbdillāh; the kunyah of Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام
key_terms.رَكْعَتَيْنِ: two rakʿahs; the two units of salat (prayer) in question
key_terms.سَأَلْتُ: I asked; indicates the direct inquiry posed to the Imam عليه السلام
key_terms.لَا يَدْرِي: he does not know; expresses uncertainty or doubt
key_terms.وَاحِدَةً: one; the alternative number of rakʿahs being doubted
key_terms.يُتِمُّ: he completes it; the ruling to continue and complete the prayer

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if he doubts whether he has prayed one rakʿah or two?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning doubt in salat (prayer), specifically when a person is unsure whether he has prayed one rakʿah or two. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام instructs that he should complete the prayer, showing a practical ruling for uncertainty in the early rakʿahs.
